L160: # Filters
L161: 
L162: Filters define trading rules on a symbol or an exchange. Filters come in three forms: `symbol filters`, `exchange filters` and `asset filters`.
L163: 
L164: ## Symbol filters
L165: ### PRICE_FILTER
L166: 
L167: The `PRICE_FILTER` defines the `price` rules for a symbol. There are 3 parts:
L168: 
L169:   * `minPrice` defines the minimum `price`/`stopPrice` allowed; disabled on `minPrice` == 0.
L170:   * `maxPrice` defines the maximum `price`/`stopPrice` allowed; disabled on `maxPrice` == 0.
L171:   * `tickSize` defines the intervals that a `price`/`stopPrice` can be increased/decreased by; disabled on `tickSize` == 0.
L172: Any of the above variables can be set to 0, which disables that rule in the `price filter`. In order to pass the `price filter`, the following must be true for `price`/`stopPrice` of the enabled rules:
L173: 
L174:   * `price` >= `minPrice`
L175:   * `price` <= `maxPrice`
L176:   * `price` % `tickSize` == 0
L177: 
L178: /exchangeInfo format:
L179: 
L180:     Code
L181: 
L182:     `{
L183:         "filterType": "PRICE_FILTER",
L184:         "minPrice": "0.00000100",
L185:         "maxPrice": "100000.00000000",
L186:         "tickSize": "0.00000100"
L187:     }`
L188: ### PERCENT_PRICE
L189: 
L190: The `PERCENT_PRICE` filter defines the valid range for an order `price` based on an `average of previous trade prices`.
L191: 
L192:   * When a non-null cite30†reference price for the symbol exists, it is used in the filter evaluation.
L193:   * When a non-null reference price for the symbol does not exist, then the volume weighted average price over the preceding `avgPriceMins` minutes is used in the filter evaluation.
L194:     * If `avgPriceMins` is 0, then the last price is used in the filter evaluation.
L195: An order will pass this filter evaluation if:
L196: 
L197:   * `price` <= `average of previous trade prices` * `multiplierUp`
L198:   * `price` >= `average of previous trade prices` * `multiplierDown`
L199: 
L200: /exchangeInfo format:
L201: 
L202:     Code
L203: 
L204:     `{
L205:         "filterType": "PERCENT_PRICE",
L206:         "multiplierUp": "1.3000",
L207:         "multiplierDown": "0.7000",
L208:         "avgPriceMins": 5
L209:     }`
L210: ### PERCENT_PRICE_BY_SIDE
L211: 
L212: The `PERCENT_PRICE_BY_SIDE` filter defines the valid range for an order `price` based on an `average of previous trade prices`.
L213:   * When a non-null cite30†reference price for the symbol exists, it is used in the filter evaluation.
L214:   * When a non-null reference price for the symbol does not exist, then the volume weighted average price over the preceding `avgPriceMins` minutes is used in the filter evaluation.
L215:     * If `avgPriceMins` is 0, then the last price is used in the filter evaluation.
L216: 
L217: There is a different range depending on whether an order is placed on the `BUY` side or the `SELL` side.
L218: A `BUY` order will pass this filter evaluation if:
L219: 
L220:   * `price` <= `average of previous trade prices` * `bidMultiplierUp`
L221:   * `price` >= `average of previous trade prices` * `bidMultiplierDown`
L222: 
L223: A `SELL` order will pass this filter evaluation if:
L224: 
L225:   * `price` <= `average of previous trade prices` * `askMultiplierUp`
L226:   * `price` >= `average of previous trade prices` * `askMultiplierDown`
L227: /exchangeInfo format:
L228: 
L229:     Code
L230: 
L231:     `{
L232:         "filterType": "PERCENT_PRICE_BY_SIDE",
L233:         "bidMultiplierUp": "1.2",
L234:         "bidMultiplierDown": "0.2",
L235:         "askMultiplierUp": "5",
L236:         "askMultiplierDown": "0.8",
L237:         "avgPriceMins": 1
L238:     }`
L239: ### LOT_SIZE
L240: 
L241: The `LOT_SIZE` filter defines the `quantity` (aka "lots" in auction terms) rules for a symbol. There are 3 parts:
L242: 
L243:   * `minQty` defines the minimum `quantity`/`icebergQty` allowed.
L244:   * `maxQty` defines the maximum `quantity`/`icebergQty` allowed.
L245:   * `stepSize` defines the intervals that a `quantity`/`icebergQty` can be increased/decreased by.

L69: ## ADL Risk
L70: 
L71: Query the symbol-level ADL risk rating.
L72: 
L73: The ADL risk rating measures the likelihood of ADL during liquidation, and the rating takes into account the insurance fund balance, position concentration on the symbol, order book depth, price volatility, average leverage, unrealized PnL, and margin utilization at the symbol level.
L74: 
L75: The rating can be high, medium and low, and is updated every 30 minutes.
L76: 
L77: GET
L78: 
L79: /fapi/v1/symbolAdlRisk
L80: 
L81: https://fapi.binance.com
L82: ### ADL Risk › Request Weight
L83: 
L84: This endpoint consumes IP-based request weight. Heavier endpoints consume more of your IP rate limit capacity.
L85: 
L86: Learn more in the cite120†Rate limits section.
L87: 
L88: IP Weight 1
L89: 
L90: ### ADL Risk › Query Parameters
L91: 
L92: `symbol`
L93: 
L94: ​string
L95: 
L96: Symbol
L97: 
L98: Example: BTCUSDT
L99: 
L100: ### ADL Risk › Responses

L24: There are three types of applicable fees in Binance Futures trading:
L25: 
L26: 1. Commission Fee (Incurred every time an order is executed)
L27: 2. Funding Fee (Incurred depending on the trade position at the time of settlement)
L28: 3. Insurance Clearance Fee (Incurred when a position is forcibly liquidated)
L29: 
L30: Read below to learn more about the different fees involved.
L31: 
L32: 1. Commission fee
L33: 
L34: The commission fee incurred on your order can vary depending on several factors:
L35: Pay-out Timing  | Whether your position was partially or fully executed
L36: VIP Levels  | Your participation and progress in our exclusive programs
L37: Maker & Taker  | Whether your order remains on the order book as a maker or is immediately matched as a taker.Maker: Orders that provide market liquidity. If you place an order that is not immediately executed and remains on the order book, commonly seen in limit orders, you are acting as a maker. This action means you are adding liquidity to the market.Taker: Orders that remove market liquidity. If you place an order that is immediately executed, like a market order, you are acting as a taker.
L38: These orders remove liquidity from the order book.
L39: BNB Discount  | Receive a 10% discount on standard trading fees when you use BNB to pay for commission fees on the Binance Futures platform for USDⓈ-M Futures. Please ensure that you have transferred a sufficient BNB balance to your USDⓈ-M Futures Wallet, otherwise the system will automatically deduct USDT for the fees and you will not be entitled to the discount.
L40: #### Commission fee calculation
L41: 
L42: Depending on the contract type, commission fees will differ in calculation:
L43: 
L44: For USDⓈ-Margined:
L45: Commission Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L46: Notional Value = Number of Contracts * Trade Price
L47: 
L48: For COIN-Margin:
L49: Commission Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L50: Notional Value = (Number of Contracts* Contract Size) / Trade Price
L51: 
L52: For more details on commission fees calculations, see the cite56†Binance Futures Fee Structure & Calculations page.
L53: 
L54: 2. Funding fee
L55: Funding rates are exchanged between long- and short-position holders periodically, to help converge perpetual contracts’ prices to underlying asset prices. Through the funding rate, traders are incentivized to hold positions that help align the contract price closer to the spot price.
L56: 
L57: Please note that Binance only helps facilitate the exchange of funding amounts between long- and short-position holders. Binance does not charge any service fees.
L58: Additionally, the funding rate can serve as an indicator of market sentiment. A positive funding rate typically indicates that long positions are stronger in the market, while a negative funding rate suggests that short positions are more dominant.
L59: #### Funding fee settlement time
L60: 
L61: Typically settling every 8 hours, the frequency of funding fee settlements varies depending on the cryptocurrency pair held.
L62: 
L63: Funding payments with a settlement frequency of every 8 hours start at 00:00 (UTC), 08:00 (UTC), and 16:00 (UTC).
L64: 
L65: Funding payments with a settlement frequency of every 4 hours start at 00:00 (UTC), 04:00 (UTC), 08:00 (UTC), 12:00 (UTC), 16:00 (UTC), and 20:00 (UTC).
L66: #### Funding fee payments and receipts
L67: 
L68: Traders will be charged or receive the funding fee only if they hold a position in the corresponding direction at the time the fee is charged. If there is no position held at that time, no funding fee will be paid or received.
L69: 
L70: The flow of funding fee payments and receipts is as follow:
L71: 
L72:    | Funding Rate > 0  | Funding Rate < 0
L73: Long position  | Paying funding fee  | Receiving funding fee
L74: Short position  | Receiving funding fee  | Paying funding fee

L19: Fellow Binancians,
L20: 
L21: Binance VIP program is evolving to better recognize the broad base of high-value users contributing to the platform, enabling us to identify and support them earlier in their journey as they deepen engagement across our ecosystem.
L22: As part of this, Binance is updating key VIP program eligibility criteria across trading and capital allocation, while ensuring tier recognition remains tied to sustained and meaningful engagement.
L23: ## VIP Program Key Changes
L24: 
L25: ### 1. Lower BNB Holding Requirements for VIP 1-3

L35: ### 2. Lower Futures Trading Requirements for VIP 1-3 with Calibrated Fees

L53: Enhanced Referral Eligibility for the Futures Referral & Affiliate Program
L54: 
L55: Effective from 2026-03-19, and in alignment with the updated Futures VIP thresholds, users will now be eligible to cite11†receive Futures commissions generated by referrals from regular to VIP 2 users, an increase from the previous cap of VIP 1.
L56: Additionally, Futures trading volume generated by referrals within this expanded VIP range will be included in Affiliates’ Futures Evaluation performance metrics.
L57: ### 3. New VIP Criteria for Holders & Investors, with Expanded Eligible VIP Levels Up to VIP 9
L58: 
L59: Users who qualify for VIP through holding or investing activities (including Binance Earn) will now follow a new eligibility framework under the cite12†Holder Program . This gives VIP users greater flexibility to allocate assets across products while maintaining the highest VIP level they qualify for.
L60: In addition, BNB holdings will now count toward both overall asset calculations and the BNB holding requirement. The updated Holder program will include assets across all Binance accounts, including Spot, Futures, Funding, Earn and Alpha.
L61: For example, if your account holds 250 BNB (assuming it is equivalent to 150,000 USD) along with other assets worth 100,000 USD, your total account asset holding will be considered as 250,000 USD and 250 BNB. This meets the VIP BNB holding requirement, making you eligible for the new Holder VIP 2 status.
L62: This update also expands eligible VIP levels for holders and investors. With this change, users can now qualify for VIP 5-9 based on asset holdings, creating a clearer pathway for long-term holders and investors to reach higher VIP levels.

L75: ### 4. Introducing the VIP Rising Star Program
L76: 
L77: We’re introducing VIP Rising Star, created to recognize and support high-potential users on their journey towards Binance VIP.
